column1: The thesis titled An Initial Study on Load Forecasting Considering Economic Factors by Hossein Sangrody and Ning Zhou from the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department at the State University of New York  Binghamton University  presents a novel approach to load forecasting (LF) by incorporating economic factors into the forecasting process. The authors propose a new objective function and utilize a quantile regression (QR) algorithm to improve the accuracy and economic efficiency of load forecasts. The paper highlights that traditional LF methods often do not differentiate between positive and negative forecasting errors  despite their differing economic impacts. Positive errors  where actual values exceed forecasted values  can lead to inadequate capacity planning and potential loss of load service  while negative errors  where actual values are less than forecasted values  can result in resource wastage due to overcapacity.

To address this  the authors introduce an economic load forecast error (ELFE) metric that assigns different economic coefficients to positive and negative errors  reflecting their distinct financial implications. The proposed methodology is applied to the long-term load forecasting (LTLF) of the net energy load (NEL) of the New England network. The results are compared with three other LF methods: time series analysis  artificial neural networks (ANN)  and support vector machines (SVM). The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method is more effective in reducing the economic cost of LF errors compared to the other methods.

The paper is structured as follows: Section I provides an introduction to the importance of LF in power system operation and planning  outlining the different time horizons for LF  from very short-term to long-term. It also reviews various LF methods  including time series analysis  machine learning  and hybrid methods  and discusses the limitations of traditional error metrics like the mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)  which do not account for the direction of errors. Section II formulates the LF problem into a new objective function  introducing the ELFE metric. Section III describes the proposed methodology  detailing the use of QR to solve the LF problem using a linear LF model. Section IV presents the simulation results  showing the effectiveness of the proposed method in reducing economic costs. Finally  Section V concludes the paper  summarizing the findings and implications of the study.

Overall  the thesis contributes to the field of load forecasting by integrating economic considerations into the forecasting process  offering a more nuanced approach that accounts for the financial impacts of forecasting errors. This approach has the potential to improve the accuracy and economic efficiency of load forecasts  ultimately benefiting power system planning and operation.
